title: Making LB Agar Plates
author: Priota Islam
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8eqhtdw

steps.title: Prepare and melt LB Agar
steps.instruction: Prepare LB Agar using 1 L of sterile H2O and 37 g of pre-mixed powder (consisting of 5 g peptone, 10 g peptone from casein, 10 g sodium chloride, and 10 g agar-agar), then autoclave to melt.

steps.title: Add antibiotics if required
steps.instruction: If bacteria have a specific antibiotic resistance, add a 1000x stock of that antibiotic to the melted LB agar before pouring.

substeps.instruction: For example, to achieve a final concentration of 100ug/ml using 100mg/ml stock ampicillin, add 200ul of stock to 200ml of LB agar.

steps.title: Pour agar plates
steps.instruction: Using sterile techniques, pour the molten agar into large (90mm) petri dishes and allow to dry overnight.

substeps.instruction: Pour roughly 30-45ml per dish (exact volume not required).
Can be used longer if not contaminated or dehydrated, but never more than 3 months.
